boston-licensing-board-late-night-smashb.title: Boston Licensing Board Weighs a Late Burger Counter, Nip Bottles and a 3 a.m. Party
boston-licensing-board-late-night-smashb.dek: In one week the Licensing Board set a 1 a.m. closing for a South Boston burger counter that had asked for 2 a.m., turned down nips in Allston, and heard from a Hyde Park owner, while the state auditor called for ending liquor-license caps.
body: Boston still closes early, and this week its Licensing Board kept it that way. Over two days in mid-October the board heard a dispute over late-night smashburgers in South Boston, rejected small liquor bottles in Allston, and questioned a Hyde Park bar owner about a party that was still going at 3 a.m., Universal Hub reported. In the same stretch, State Auditor Diana DiZoglio released a report arguing that the system that lets a Boston liquor license cost up to $600,000 should be dismantled, according to WBUR.
## "We Do Sleep Here in Boston"

7th Street Burger, a New York take-out smashburger chain that opened in April at 475 West Broadway in Perkins Square, asked to move its closing time from 11 p.m. to 2 a.m., Universal Hub reported. Residents and City Councilor Ed Flynn opposed the request.

Ellen Fritch, who lives on Silver Street, told the board she already has trouble sleeping after midnight because of loud bar patrons. "New York is the city that doesn't sleep," she said, "but we do sleep here in Boston," according to Universal Hub. Amanda Jerome, another resident, pointed to wrapper litter and to delivery drivers riding scooters. Flynn, speaking through an aide, cited noise, pedestrian safety and pest control.

Tom Miller, the company's attorney, said the chain usually stays open until 3 or 4 a.m. at its other locations without trouble, that it serves shift workers, students and hotel guests, and that with no seats inside, customers do not linger, Universal Hub reported. Chairwoman Kathleen Joyce called the company a good operator but said she was concerned about congestion on Broadway when the bars let out.

On Oct. 15 the board settled on 1 a.m., a compromise the business itself offered after the hearing, according to Universal Hub. It cannot return to ask for 2 a.m. for at least a year. Joyce said she wanted the business to "build trust with the neighbors."

The same hearing took up a request from Achilitos Taqueria to move into the former Little Stevie's space on Boylston Street in the Fenway, with hours until 2 a.m. most nights and 2:30 a.m. on weekends. No one spoke against it, Universal Hub reported.
## No Nips on Comm. Ave.

In Allston, Commonwealth Cellars, at 1229 Commonwealth Ave. near Harvard Avenue, asked permission to sell nip-sized liquor bottles. The board rejected the request with prejudice on Oct. 15, which means owner Wondimu Abeje must wait at least a year before applying again, Universal Hub reported.

Conor Newman, deputy director of the Mayor's Office of Neighborhood Services, argued that public drinking is an ongoing problem in Allston Village and that nip sales would add to it. The Allston Civic Association also opposed the request. "I don't think it makes sense in this particular area," Joyce said, according to Universal Hub.
## The 3 a.m. Birthday

The board also questioned George Craan, owner of Little Haiti International Cuisine at 1184 Hyde Park Ave., about a July 5 visit in which a police sergeant found people inside with music playing at 3 a.m., Universal Hub reported. Craan said about 15 relatives from Connecticut, there for a 50th birthday, were afraid to leave separately after reports of shootings on July 4. "Your name is on this license," Joyce told him. The bar's hours had already been cut back to 9:30 p.m. after a fatal shooting outside on Aug. 3.
## The Auditor's Case

DiZoglio's 181-page report says the state's population-based caps on liquor licenses create an artificial scarcity, WBUR reported. A license can cost up to $600,000 in Boston and $175,000 in Somerville, but about $2,500 in Cambridge, which controls its own licensing, according to the report. Communities with local control issued twice as many licenses per capita as communities under the caps.

"We need a liquor licensing system that is transparent, fair and gives all of our local businesses a shot at success," DiZoglio said, according to WBUR. Steve Clark of the Massachusetts Restaurant Association said owners regard their licenses as valuable assets, and he suggested a buyback program. Language ending the caps is in the Senate's economic development bill, which is still being negotiated; Gov. Maura Healey supports lifting them, while some House leaders have raised concerns, WBUR reported.

womens-sports-bar-the-sports-bra-readies.title: Women's Sports Bar The Sports Bra Prepares to Open Downtown
womens-sports-bar-the-sports-bra-readies.dek: Eight Boston locals are finishing work on a Broad Street space for the franchise, a bar that shows only women's sports.
body: The Sports Bra, a sports bar that shows only women's sports, is getting ready to open its Boston location at 2 Broad St. in the Financial District, according to Boston.com.
The 3,243-square-foot space was once home to Tiki Rock, Boston.com reported. There is no opening date yet, only a sign on the door that reads "Game time: Fall 2026."

Inside there will be a large seating area and TVs carrying local and national women's games, among them Boston Legacy FC of the NWSL, the Boston Fleet of the PWHL and the Boston Hunters of the WPBL, according to the report. The owners said the bar will be family-friendly and will favor local, women-owned businesses as suppliers.

The franchise belongs to eight Boston friends whose idea began in a group chat, Boston.com reported. In 2024 they started Watch With Us Boston, which held pop-up watch parties, and in early 2025 they signed a franchise agreement. Owner Lydia Coverdale-Perez said the group saw the space as the right fit, and spokesperson Dana Marie Cincis described the bar as a community hub for women's sports.

The first Sports Bra opened in Portland, Oregon, in 2022. Founder Jenny Nguyen announced in 2025 that it would expand to Boston and to Portland, Maine, and she praised the leadership of the Boston ownership group, according to Boston.com.

the-sports-bra-franchise-announces-bosto.title: The Sports Bra Franchise Announces Financial District Location
the-sports-bra-franchise-announces-bosto.dek: The women's sports bar chain, which started in Portland, Oregon, will open in the old Tiki Rock space on Broad Street, the Boston Globe reported.
body: The Sports Bra, a franchise billed as the first sports bar given over entirely to women's sports, has announced a Boston location at 2 Broad St. in the Financial District, the Boston Globe reported.
Renovations at the 3,243-square-foot former Tiki Rock space are almost finished, according to the Globe, though no opening date has been set. A sign on the door reads "Game time: Fall 2026."

The bar will have a large bar area and TVs showing local and national women's sports, including the Boston Legacy, the Boston Fleet and the Boston Hunters, the Globe reported. It is meant to be family-friendly, with a broad food and drink menu and an emphasis on products from local, women-owned businesses.

The Boston franchise is owned by eight friends from the Boston area who formed Watch With Us Boston in 2024 to host pop-up watch parties, according to the Globe. As the crowds grew they went looking for a permanent room, and in early 2025 they signed with The Sports Bra. Spokesperson Dana Marie Cincis said the aim is a community hub for women's sports history, education and visibility.
The first Sports Bra opened in Portland, Oregon, in 2022. Founder Jenny Nguyen announced the franchise expansion in 2025, including Boston and Portland, Maine.

bloom-a-cafe-by-day-and-cocktail-bar-by-.title: Bloom, a Matcha Cafe by Day and Cocktail Bar by Night, Opens in the Seaport
bloom-a-cafe-by-day-and-cocktail-bar-by-.dek: The 20-seat room at 60 Seaport Blvd. pours tea in the daytime and cocktails in the evening, according to Boston.com.
body: Bloom, a 20-seat tea cafe that becomes a craft cocktail bar after dark, was set to open Oct. 6 in the Seaport, Boston.com reported. It sits in the atrium at 60 Seaport Blvd., in the space Zazibar used to occupy.

According to the report, Bloom serves matcha and hojicha from 11 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., then cocktails from 5 p.m. to 11 p.m. It will be closed Mondays for its first two weeks before moving to seven days, with limited hours and a shorter menu at the start.

Christian Doan, an investor in the nearby izakaya Mai, is leading the project with Mai partner Ray Lee, who has run tea shops in Boston for about two decades, and co-founder Isabelle Lin, Boston.com reported. Chef Chompon Boonnak of Mahaniyom and Merai, Markus Yao, formerly of Shojo, and bartender Iruma Shibuya are also part of it, according to the report.

The daytime menu offers matcha flights, genmaicha and aged teas, most of them from MEM Tea in Cambridge, the report said. In the evening there are classic cocktails, a martini service with Japanese and Vietnamese gins, a matcha version of the espresso martini, and a shochu highball infused with shiso and kombu. A food menu of milk bread sandwiches, curry rice bowls and bar snacks is still to come, according to Boston.com.

The Bangkok firm Minick\Bom designed the space with wood, greenery and lantern-style lighting drawn from Japanese botanical gardens, the report said. The owners told Boston.com they wanted a room centered on nature, set against the corporate feel of the Seaport.

blood-manor-haunted-attraction-2026-seas.title: Blood Manor, Billed as New York's Largest Haunted Attraction, Opens for 2026
blood-manor-haunted-attraction-2026-seas.dek: Blood Manor runs through Nov. 7 in Manhattan and this season adds a $350 Scare Actor Academy that lets guests work as performers, amNY reported.
body: Blood Manor, billed as New York's largest haunted attraction, has returned to Manhattan for the 2026 season. It draws thousands of guests through a landmarked building, and the owner says the landlord has been supportive, according to amNY.
The attraction is open through Nov. 7. General admission starts at $50, with student discounts on certain days, and tickets are sold online, amNY reported.
## The Performers
Jim Lorenzo, the owner and creator, told amNY that Blood Manor will remain at its current location for as long as the lease allows.
> "We try to keep a location for as long as we possibly can." — Jim Lorenzo, Blood Manor

Some of the performers have been there for years. Sammy Mena, known to regulars as the Blood Manor Clown, has been scaring guests there since 2006. Another performer, Yum Yum, stands at the entrance. Mena told amNY that the cast likes to torment everyone waiting outside.

The cast is the center of the house. Mena, there since 2006, is among its longest-serving performers, and his routine starts before guests reach the door, aimed at the people still in line, according to amNY.
## The Scare Actor Academy

This year Blood Manor added another way in. Its Scare Actor Academy lets guests move to the other side and work as scare actors themselves. The $350 ticket includes a professional costume and makeup, and one of the instructors is a performer known as the Countess, according to amNY.
Lorenzo told the publication that his favorite thing about this year's house is the same thing that has been his favorite every year.
## A Night for a Cause

On Oct. 27, Blood Manor will hold its fourth annual charity event with Z100. The night honors Lorenzo's son, Joey, who died of cancer six years ago, and donations go to St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, amNY reported.
## Planning a Visit

Tickets are sold online, with general admission from $50 and student discounts on select days. The season closes Nov. 7, a week after Halloween, and Lorenzo expects about the same attendance as past years, when the house drew thousands of guests, amNY reported.

1tbsp-plays-all-night-at-nowadays-oct-22.title: 1tbsp Plays All-Night Set at Nowadays on Oct. 22
1tbsp-plays-all-night-at-nowadays-oct-22.dek: The Brisbane-born dance project 1tbsp plays a sold-out all-night set at the Ridgewood club Nowadays on Thursday, Oct. 22.
body: On Thursday, Oct. 22, Nowadays gives the whole night to 1tbsp, according to the event's Resident Advisor listing. The party runs from 9 p.m. to 3 a.m. at the club at 56-06 Cooper Ave. in Ridgewood, Queens.

According to the listing, 1tbsp is the touring dance project of a Grammy-nominated songwriter and producer from Brisbane, Australia, who also records as Golden Vessel. The listing describes the sound as indie-house and dance music that blends warmth, leftfield ideas and pop melody, and says the project grew out of parties the artist first threw in Brisbane.

Tickets started at $20 and are now listed as sold out, with a resale queue running and online purchases limited to four per person. The event is 21 and over. Nowadays says it sometimes keeps tickets back for the door, but entry without one is not guaranteed and admission is up to staff.

The club's listing says harassment, violence and discriminatory behavior are not tolerated. Wheelchair access is through the driveway, which stays locked during parties, so guests are asked to check with staff at the street entrance. Bathrooms are gender-neutral, with one accessible indoor stall, and the booths, the deck and the backyard offer quieter places to step away. The club notes that its parties usually use strobe lights and water-based haze.

nowadays-nonstop-runs-oct-24-with-ayesha.title: Nowadays Nonstop Runs Overnight Oct. 24 With Ayesha, Mor Elian and Pearson Sound
nowadays-nonstop-runs-oct-24-with-ayesha.dek: The Ridgewood club's Nonstop party starts at 10 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 24, and runs until 3 p.m. the next day.
body: Nowadays opens its Nonstop marathon at 10 p.m. on Saturday, Oct. 24, and keeps going until 3 p.m. Sunday, according to the event's Resident Advisor listing. The club is at 56-06 Cooper Ave. in Ridgewood, Queens.

The listed schedule starts with Arthur from 10 p.m. to 1 a.m., then Tasha until 3 a.m., The Untouchables until 5 a.m., BEARCAT until 7 a.m. and Baby Leo until 9 a.m. Ayesha and Mor Elian play back to back until noon, and Pearson Sound closes from noon to 3 p.m. The listing tags the night as drum and bass and bass music, with sets that move from dub and hardgroove to jungle and faster styles.

Tickets are listed from $25. RSVPs cost $10 before 11 p.m. and $15 before midnight, cover one person each and do not guarantee entry, according to the listing. Tickets are tied to entry windows, re-entry depends on capacity, and online purchases are capped at four per person. The event is 21 and over.

Those still inside can also get into the Mister Sunday party in the club's backyard starting at 3 p.m., the listing says. Nowadays lists a safer-space policy, gender-neutral bathrooms with one accessible indoor stall, and wheelchair access through the driveway.

mister-sunday-brings-floating-points-and.title: Mister Sunday Hosts Floating Points and Justin Carter at Nowadays Oct. 25
mister-sunday-brings-floating-points-and.dek: Floating Points joins resident Justin Carter for the daytime party's second-to-last session of the season in Ridgewood.
body: Floating Points joins resident Justin Carter at Mister Sunday on Sunday, Oct. 25, at Nowadays in Ridgewood, Queens, according to the event's Resident Advisor listing. The listing calls it the second-to-last party of the season.

According to the listed schedule, Carter plays from 3 p.m. to 6 p.m., Floating Points follows from 6 p.m. to 8 p.m., and the two finish the day back to back from 8 p.m. to 9 p.m. The party takes place at the club at 56-06 Cooper Ave., and doors close at 8:30 p.m. The listing calls Floating Points a long-time friend of the party. The event is presented by Mister Sunday and Nowadays.

The listing does not give a base ticket price. RSVP holders get $10 off the door charge before 4 p.m. and $5 off before 5 p.m., and RSVPs close an hour before the party starts. Early-entry tickets are good from 3 p.m. to 4 p.m.; after that, entry depends on capacity, according to the listing.

Organizers ask people to put their phones away and dance. The listing says the outdoor space has both sun and shade, along with Mexican food, free water, and drinks with and without alcohol. Organizers also offer a way to get in touch for anyone facing financial hardship who needs help getting in, and the listing lays out a conduct policy against violence, harassment and discrimination.

hercules-love-affair-dustin-zahn-and-eli.title: Hercules & Love Affair, Dustin Zahn and Eli Escobar Play Basement Oct. 24
hercules-love-affair-dustin-zahn-and-eli.dek: The Maspeth club's sold-out Saturday splits techno and house acts between its Basement and Studio rooms.
body: Basement, the club at 52-19 Flushing Ave. in Maspeth, Queens, has a two-room night on Saturday, Oct. 24, from 10:30 p.m. to 7 a.m., according to the event's Resident Advisor listing. It is listed as sold out, with a resale queue running, and is 21 and over.

The main Basement room has Dustin Zahn, described in the listing as a veteran Midwest techno DJ returning to the club; Kameliia, a Bulgarian-born DJ and producer coming back after her debut there in April; and Ade Kassim, a New York artist making his first appearance with a mix of techno and sound art.

In the Studio room, Hercules & Love Affair headline with a set the listing says draws on classic house music. With them are Eli Escobar, a selector and member of Tiki Disco, and Andi, founder of Synthecide, whose sets center on 1980s dance, goth, industrial and pop, according to the listing.

House rules prohibit photos, videos and phone use on the dance floor, require consent, and bar discrimination of any kind, the listing says. About 1,400 people had marked interest in the night on Resident Advisor.

fist-takes-over-basement-friday-oct-23.title: FIST Party Takes Over Basement in Maspeth on Oct. 23
fist-takes-over-basement-friday-oct-23.dek: Techno producer Lacchesi headlines the FIST party at Basement on Friday, Oct. 23, with a second lineup in the club's Studio room.
body: The FIST party comes to Basement, at 52-19 Flushing Ave. in Maspeth, Queens, on Friday, Oct. 23, from 10:30 p.m. to 7 a.m., according to the event's Resident Advisor listing. FIST and Basement present the night, and it is 21 and over.

Lacchesi headlines the main Basement room. The listing describes his techno as cinematic and slow to build, with a hard edge tied to late-1990s classics. He is joined by Nene H, a Turkish-Azerbaijani artist whose 2026 release "Second Skin" the listing presents as a breakthrough, and by party residents Word of Command and DJ Clone.

The Studio room has Jubilee, a Florida-based label founder known for electro, grime and dancehall; Mez Monty, a Los Angeles house DJ whose sets lean on diva vocals; and Connor Wrong, whose sets range across psy, house, bass and grime, according to the listing.

The listing did not show ticket prices. House rules ban photos, videos and phone use on the dance floor, require consent and prohibit discrimination, and anyone who breaks them is removed. The listing notes that a ticket does not guarantee admission. About 317 people had marked interest in the night.

ultra-nate-headlines-paradiso-at-paragon.title: Ultra Naté Headlines Paradiso at Paragon in Brooklyn Oct. 23
ultra-nate-headlines-paradiso-at-paragon.dek: Paragon's Paradiso night on Friday, Oct. 23, has Ultra Naté at the top of a bill with Kilopatrah Jones, Karim Olen Ash, Saia and RATONC1T0.
body: Ultra Naté headlines Paradiso at Paragon, the club at 990 Broadway in Brooklyn, on Friday, Oct. 23, according to the event's Resident Advisor listing. The night runs from 9:30 p.m. to 3 a.m.
Kilopatrah Jones, Karim Olen Ash, Saia and RATONC1T0 are also on the lineup, the listing shows. Resident Advisor tags the night as techno and house, and Paragon is presenting it.
Tickets are listed at $25 through Resident Advisor, and the event is 21 and over. About 149 users had marked interest as of the listing.

In its event notes, Paragon tells guests to come early to avoid lines and to dress up, and says its ground floor is ADA compliant. The club's code of conduct prohibits racism, sexism, discrimination and violence, and asks anyone who sees harassment to tell security.
The listing did not say whether the night was close to selling out.

effy-plays-h0l0-friday-oct-23.title: UK DJ Effy Plays H0L0 in Ridgewood on Oct. 23
effy-plays-h0l0-friday-oct-23.dek: The British producer and DJ Effy is the only act on the bill at H0L0 on Friday, Oct. 23.
body: UK producer and DJ Effy plays H0L0, the club at 1090 Wyckoff Ave. in Ridgewood, Queens, on Friday, Oct. 23, according to the event's Resident Advisor listing. The night runs from 10 p.m. to 4 a.m., and she has it to herself.

MeanRed Productions and H0L0 present the night, which is tagged as techno and tech house. It is 21 and over. The listing did not show ticket prices and says group rates are available by contacting the promoter on social media. About 130 people had marked interest.

According to the biography in the listing, Effy, whose name is Sophie Cooper, is a producer, DJ, radio host and label founder from the North West of England. She released her first single in 2020 and has held a residency on Rinse FM. She has played clubs and festivals including Fabric, Parklife, The Warehouse Project and Amnesia in Ibiza, the listing says.

Her debut EP, Not What It Seems, came out in 2022, and tours of Australia, Japan and Europe followed. The listing also cites a Boiler Room set in Sydney and her track "iluv," released on Fragrance Recordings, the label she runs with Mall Grab. Her 2025 EP, The Syndicate, is a tribute to Blackpool and the North West, according to the listing.

a-day-in-tulum-music-and-arts-festival-a.title: 'A Day in Tulum' Rooftop Party Comes to Superior Ingredients Oct. 25
a-day-in-tulum-music-and-arts-festival-a.dek: The promoter Tropique holds a daytime rooftop music and arts event at the Williamsburg venue on Sunday, Oct. 25.
body: A daytime rooftop event billed as the A Day in Tulum Music and Arts Festival takes place at Superior Ingredients, 74 Wythe Ave. in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, on Sunday, Oct. 25, according to the event's Resident Advisor listing. It runs from 2 p.m. to 10 p.m.

The promoter Tropique is presenting it. According to the listing, the aim is to recreate the experience of Tulum, Mexico, with house music, Mexican-inspired food, craft cocktails, art and live performances, with the Manhattan skyline behind the venue's rooftop.

The listed lineup includes FI-LO, Robidio, Kuff, Santo and Jason Merced, along with paired sets from Manuela and Its V1B3 and from Anthony Micele and Mike Tomlinson. Resident Advisor tags the music as minimal and Afro tech.
Admission is listed at $25, and the event is 21 and over. The listing shows no other ticket tiers. As of its last update, two Resident Advisor users had marked interest.

floating-points-headlines-refuge-saturda.title: Floating Points Headlines Refuge Saturday Oct. 24
floating-points-headlines-refuge-saturda.dek: The British producer Floating Points tops the bill at Refuge's Saturday night party in Brooklyn on Oct. 24.
body: Floating Points headlines Refuge on Saturday, Oct. 24, according to an event listing on The Best Parties. The night belongs to the Brooklyn club's regular Saturday series.
Doors open at 10 p.m., and the party goes until 5 a.m. Sunday, the listing says. Refuge is at 366 Ten Eyck Street in Brooklyn.

Floating Points is the only artist named, and the listing gives no full lineup or set times. The night is tagged as house and techno, and the series is promoted with the tagline "Before. During. Afters."
The listing posts no ticket price or age policy. Tickets are sold through Eventbrite, according to the page.

victor-calderone-leads-refuges-halloween.title: Victor Calderone Leads Refuge's All-Day Halloween Party Oct. 31
victor-calderone-leads-refuges-halloween.dek: Refuge in Brooklyn opens at 6 a.m. on Halloween for a 16-hour session with Victor Calderone and Anthony Middleton.
body: Refuge holds an all-day party on Saturday, Oct. 31, with DJs Victor Calderone and Anthony Middleton, according to an event listing on The Best Parties.
Billed as PURGATORY: Saturday All Day, it starts at 6 a.m. and runs until 10 p.m., the listing says. It takes place at the club at 366 Ten Eyck Street in Brooklyn.

The session is one part of a longer Halloween run at the club that the listing describes as six parties over four days. Other listings on the same site point to a PURGATORY sunrise session that follows at Refuge on Sunday morning.
Calderone and Middleton are the only artists named, and the event is tagged as house and techno. The listing gives no ticket price or age policy. Tickets are sold through Eventbrite.

circoloco-halloween-weekend-closes-out-b.title: Circoloco Halloween Weekend Set as Final Nights at Brooklyn Storehouse
circoloco-halloween-weekend-closes-out-b.dek: The two-night party on Oct. 30 and 31 is listed as sold out, as the Navy Yard venue prepares to close and its promoter faces a court order.
body: Circoloco's Halloween weekend at Brooklyn Storehouse, inside the Brooklyn Navy Yard, runs Oct. 30 and 31, and the Friday night is listed as sold out on The Best Parties. That night runs from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m., the listing says.

The first night's lineup includes Mochakk, Beltran, Rampa, Carlita and Seth Troxler, and the Halloween night has ANOTR, Dixon, Rossi. and Jimi Jules, among others, EDM Identity reported in August. Circoloco and Teksupport present both nights.
Brooklyn Storehouse closes after Oct. 31, Resident Advisor reported. It opened in 2024 as a temporary space inside the Navy Yard, according to EDM Identity.

Resident Advisor also reported on Oct. 7 that a New Jersey court had ordered TCE Presents, the parent company of Teksupport, to cease operations, which bars it from holding events under its brands starting Nov. 7. At the time, the outlet said it was unclear whether the Oct. 30 and 31 parties would go ahead. Ticket holders should check with the seller, DICE, for updates.

kaytranada-plays-pacha-nyc-halloween-eve.title: Kaytranada Plays Pacha NYC on Halloween Eve
kaytranada-plays-pacha-nyc-halloween-eve.dek: The producer headlines the Brooklyn club on Friday, Oct. 30, with tickets starting at about $222.
body: Kaytranada headlines Pacha NYC on Friday, Oct. 30, according to an event listing on The Best Parties. The show runs from 10 p.m. to 4 a.m.
The club is at 140 Stewart Avenue in Brooklyn, the listing says. Pacha New York relaunched in Brooklyn in June as the first North American outpost of the Ibiza-based club brand, Resident reported.
Kaytranada is the only artist listed for the night, which is tagged as electronic. Tickets start at about $222, according to the listing.

The club held a pre-opening weekend on June 13 and 14 curated by Rampa, and its fall calendar has included BLOND:ISH in September, with a Miss Monique night set for Nov. 13, Resident reported. The Best Parties listing also points readers toward an all-day PURGATORY party at Refuge in Brooklyn the next morning.
The page gives no age policy and no set times.

purple-disco-machine-plays-pacha-nyc-on-.title: Purple Disco Machine Plays Pacha NYC on Halloween Night
purple-disco-machine-plays-pacha-nyc-on-.dek: The German producer headlines the Brooklyn club on Saturday, Oct. 31, with tickets from about $169.
body: Purple Disco Machine headlines Pacha NYC on Saturday, Oct. 31, according to an event listing on The Best Parties. The party runs from 10 p.m. to 4 a.m.
The club is at 140 Stewart Avenue in Brooklyn, the listing says. Pacha New York opened in Brooklyn in June as the Ibiza-based brand's first club in North America, Resident reported.
Purple Disco Machine is the only artist named for the night, which is tagged as electronic. Tickets start at about $169, according to the listing.

The page gives no age policy or set times. The Halloween date comes the night after a Kaytranada show at the same club on Friday, Oct. 30, and ahead of a Miss Monique night there on Nov. 13, according to Resident.

lost-frequencies-plays-marquee-new-york-.title: Lost Frequencies Plays Marquee New York Oct. 30
lost-frequencies-plays-marquee-new-york-.dek: The Belgian DJ headlines the Chelsea club on the Friday before Halloween; entry is 21 and over.
body: Lost Frequencies plays Marquee New York on Friday, Oct. 30, according to an event listing on The Best Parties. The night runs from 11 p.m. to 4 a.m.
Marquee is at 289 10th Avenue in Chelsea, the listing says. Lost Frequencies is the only artist named on the bill, and the night is tagged as hip-hop and open format.
Entry is by table reservation or general admission, and guests must be 21 or older, according to the listing. No ticket price is posted. Tickets are sold through a link on the listing.

The next night, Saturday, Oct. 31, the club holds a Halloween party headlined by the DJ duo Two Friends, according to a separate listing on the same site. For anyone carrying on into the weekend, the listing points to an all-day PURGATORY party at Refuge in Brooklyn with Victor Calderone and Anthony Middleton, from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. on Saturday.

two-friends-headline-marquee-new-york-on.title: Two Friends Headline Marquee New York on Halloween
two-friends-headline-marquee-new-york-on.dek: The DJ duo plays the Chelsea club on Saturday, Oct. 31, from 11 p.m.; entry is 21 and over.
body: The DJ duo Two Friends headlines Marquee New York on Halloween night, Saturday, Oct. 31, according to an event listing on The Best Parties. The night runs from 11 p.m. until 4 a.m. on Nov. 1.
Marquee is at 289 10th Avenue in Chelsea, the listing says. Two Friends is the only act named for the night, which is tagged as hip-hop and open format.
Entry is by table reservation or general admission, and guests must be 21 or older, according to the listing. The page posts no ticket price. Tickets are sold through the Tao Group ticketing site.

The Halloween show follows a set at the club on Friday, Oct. 30, by the Belgian DJ Lost Frequencies. The listing also points to a PURGATORY sunrise session with Mira at Refuge in Brooklyn, from 6 a.m. to noon on Sunday.

court-orders-teksupport-and-parent-firm-.title: Court Orders Teksupport and Parent Firm to Cease Operations After Nov. 7
court-orders-teksupport-and-parent-firm-.dek: A New Jersey court order requires TCE Presents, parent of the New York party promoter Teksupport, to stop holding events and liquidate its assets.
body: A New Jersey court has ordered TCE Presents, the parent company of the New York promoter Teksupport, to stop holding events under any of its brands starting Nov. 7, Resident Advisor reported.
The order, filed Oct. 5, requires that non-essential TCE employees be terminated by Oct. 9, that the company's assets be liquidated and that related entities be frozen, according to RA.

It follows a dispute between Robert Toma and Michael Vitacco, who founded TCE together in 2010, RA reported. Earlier this year each filed a lawsuit in New Jersey accusing the other of undermining his role, and both are seeking sole ownership and damages. In March a court granted Vitacco a temporary restraining order barring Toma from interfering with operations, and the two have been in mediation since.

Teksupport is known for warehouse parties and for bringing European nightlife brands such as Time Warp, CircoLoco and DGTL to New York. It still has events on the calendar at Brooklyn Storehouse on Oct. 30 and 31 and at The Chocolate Factory on Nov. 6, and RA said it was unclear whether they will happen. Brooklyn Storehouse, run jointly by TCE Presents and Broadwick Live, has said it will close after Oct. 31.
RA said it had asked TCE Presents for comment and had not heard back by publication.

ticketing-company-posh-to-open-its-first.title: Ticketing Company Posh to Open Its First New York Venue
ticketing-company-posh-to-open-its-first.dek: A job posting shows the nightlife ticketing firm plans a brick-and-mortar space as a prototype for a national concept.
body: Posh, a New York-based ticketing company that focuses on nightlife events, plans to open a venue in the city, its first brick-and-mortar space, Resident Advisor reported, citing a public LinkedIn job post from Oct. 2.

According to the post, the venue will host public and private events and will be offered as an exclusive perk to Posh's top promoters, RA reported. The company wants the venue to break even each month in its first year, and the space is described as a prototype for a concept meant to go nationwide.
The name and location have not been announced, and it is not confirmed whether the venue will use Posh's own ticketing service, according to RA.

Posh is seven years old, works in major U.S. cities and is backed by several venture capital investors, RA reported. It calls itself a social networking platform and shows users the events their friends and mutual connections attend.
RA said it had contacted Posh for more information. The report carried no statement from the company.

gop-lt-gov-nominee-shawn-oliver-suspends.title: GOP Lieutenant Governor Nominee Shawn Oliver Suspends Campaign After OUI Charge
gop-lt-gov-nominee-shawn-oliver-suspends.dek: New Bedford police say the Republican nominee hit five parked cars and overturned his vehicle; his own running mate had called on him to step aside, 16 days before the election.
body: With 16 days left before Election Day, the Republican candidate for lieutenant governor of Massachusetts is no longer running. Shawn Oliver, a New Bedford city councilor, suspended his campaign on Sunday, Oct. 18, after he was charged with drunken driving, GBH News reported.

The New Bedford Police Department said Oliver crashed into five parked vehicles and overturned his car late Saturday night, according to GBH. Police took him to St. Luke's Hospital, where he was arrested and charged.

He is charged with operating under the influence of liquor, negligent operation of a motor vehicle, a marked lanes violation and speeding, GBH reported. The charges are allegations. No court outcome had been reported as of Sunday.
## The Statement, and the Call to Step Aside

Oliver announced the suspension in a statement released Sunday afternoon. He said the election was too important to be overshadowed by personal matters and asked that his family's privacy be respected, according to GBH.

The call to step aside had come from the top of his own ticket. Mike Minogue, the Republican nominee for governor, had urged Oliver to suspend his campaign immediately, GBH reported. Minogue said he was "extremely disappointed."
> "Shawn is a father and grandfather, and he needs to put his family first." — Mike Minogue, Republican nominee for governor
In the same Sunday statement, Minogue turned to Gov. Maura Healey. "That starts with accountability, something Massachusetts has not seen from Maura Healey," he said, according to GBH.
## How He Reached the Ballot

Oliver's place on the ticket came out of an unusual year. A longtime corrections officer, born and raised in New Bedford, he won the city's Ward 3 council seat in February 2023, WBUR reported in September, citing State House News Service.

Republican gubernatorial candidate Brian Shortsleeve picked Oliver as his running mate in March. After that, the other candidates fell away. According to WBUR, Anne Brensley, the candidate Minogue backed, did not meet the ballot signature threshold after a problem with fraudulent signature gathering, and Anne Manning Martin was removed from the ballot over fraudulent signatures after a complaint from Oliver. That left Oliver as the only Republican still running for lieutenant governor, and he won the Sept. 1 primary.
Shortsleeve then lost the governor's primary to Minogue, and Oliver was paired with a running mate he had not chosen. After the primary, Oliver called for party unity, WBUR reported.
## The Debate, One Week Earlier

Less than a week before the crash, Oliver faced Democratic Lt. Gov. Kim Driscoll in the campaign's only lieutenant governor debate, broadcast live on GBH's "Boston Public Radio," according to WBUR and State House News Service.

There, Oliver argued that the Healey administration had hurt the state by refusing to work with President Donald Trump, and he called for cooperation with federal law enforcement on immigration. On last month's multiday surge of Immigration and Customs Enforcement arrests in his home city, he said, "Nobody should be in fear of coming out of their house," WBUR reported. He called himself a "pro-choice Republican" and said he is the child of an immigrant mother from the Azores.
He also spoke of a "new friendship" with Minogue. "We are in constant communication," he said, according to WBUR.
## What Comes Next

Voting has already started. More than 600,000 mail-in ballots had gone out by the week of Oct. 15, and another 300,000 were waiting to be delivered, according to the office of Secretary of the Commonwealth Bill Galvin, as reported by WBUR. In-person early voting opened Saturday, Oct. 17, the same day as the crash.

GBH's report did not say whether the Massachusetts Republican Party would try to replace Oliver on the ballot, or whether that can be done this close to the Nov. 3 election. Healey and Driscoll are seeking a second term.

healey-minogue-final-debate-cook-state-p.title: Healey and Minogue Clash Over Accountability, ICE and Costs in Final Debate
healey-minogue-final-debate-cook-state-p.dek: The last televised debate of the governor's race turned on a fired aide's arrest, a State Police case and the federal immigration crackdown.
body: The last debate of the Massachusetts governor's race was a hard one. Gov. Maura Healey and Republican challenger Mike Minogue met Thursday night, Oct. 15, at WCVB's studio in Needham and argued over affordability, immigration and who should answer for the state's recent scandals, according to WBUR, NBC Boston and Boston.com.

WCVB, WBUR and the Boston Globe hosted the debate, with El Planeta and the Bay State Banner, WBUR reported. Independent candidate Andrea James, who has polled in the low single digits, was not invited.
## "In the Real World"

Minogue, a first-time candidate and former CEO of the medical device maker Abiomed, came in pressing on accountability, Boston.com reported. The day before, federal prosecutors had arrested LaMar Cook, Healey's former deputy director for Western Massachusetts, on SNAP and wire fraud charges. Cook had already been charged in October 2025 with cocaine trafficking and firearm offenses.

Healey said she fired Cook immediately. Minogue answered, as reported by Boston.com: "If someone's arrested, they're automatically fired in the real world." He also criticized the roughly $22,000 Cook was paid for unused vacation time, according to NBC Boston and State House News Service. After the debate, Healey said, "I wish I never hired LaMar Cook," NBC Boston reported.
## "Sometimes Things Happen"

The two also argued over a State Police internal affairs case in which a civilian, reportedly invited by a trooper to stay overnight at a barracks on Martha's Vineyard, is accused of raping a woman there, according to NBC Boston. Healey defended State Police Col. Geoffrey Noble.
> "Sometimes things happen, but I can tell you, he and I make sure that swift action is taken." — Gov. Maura Healey, as quoted by NBC Boston
Minogue said "sometimes things happen" is not acceptable, and that "a woman was raped," WBUR reported. Healey pointed out that the accused man is a civilian, not a trooper, according to Boston.com.
## ICE and the Federal Fight

Healey tied her opponent to President Donald Trump again and again, naming Trump 13 times by WBUR's count. On immigration, she defended the limits on state cooperation with Immigration and Customs Enforcement. "The problem is ICE," she said, according to WBUR, adding that people are afraid to go to school because of the agency.

Minogue said he would work with ICE to remove criminals and urged leaders to "lower the temperature," WBUR reported. He argued that coordination among local, state and federal authorities helps stop drug dealers, according to Boston.com.
## Gas Taxes, Pipelines and Permits

Both candidates support suspending the state gas tax, though not for the same length of time, NBC Boston reported. Minogue blamed high utility bills on Healey's opposition to natural gas pipelines and proposed cutting utility fees by a third. Healey backed what she called an "all of the above" energy approach and said Minogue "will kill wind right now," according to Boston.com.

On housing, Minogue said Massachusetts ranks last in the nation in building permits per person and proposed 45-day permit timelines, WBUR reported. Healey said the state has already cut its own permit review to 30 days, and pointed to 100,000 homes built or in development.

On abortion, Minogue, who calls himself pro-life, said he would follow state law but did not say whether he supports a 2028 ballot effort to repeal a law easing restrictions after 24 weeks, NBC Boston reported. "I trust women and their doctors. Mike Minogue doesn't," Healey said, according to Boston.com. Minogue called that a "cheap shot," WBUR reported.
## Where the Race Stands

September polls by MassINC Polling and the UNH Survey Center had Healey above 50% and Minogue below 40%, according to WBUR. Paul Watanabe, a political scientist at UMass Boston, told WBUR that Minogue "proved to be more than just his ads" but did not set out a broader agenda.
Minogue closed by calling the election a "tipping point," NBC Boston reported. The election is Nov. 3.

former-healey-aide-lamar-cook-snap-fraud.title: Former Healey Aide LaMar Cook Jailed After Federal SNAP Fraud Arrest
former-healey-aide-lamar-cook-snap-fraud.dek: Already awaiting trial on cocaine trafficking charges, the governor's former deputy for Western Massachusetts is accused of collecting food aid while hiding income, and a judge revoked his bail.
body: LaMar Cook was already awaiting trial on cocaine trafficking and gun charges. This week federal prosecutors added fraud charges, and a state judge sent him back to jail, according to WBUR, Axios Boston and Boston.com.

Cook, 46, of Springfield, was Gov. Maura Healey's deputy director for Western Massachusetts until October 2025, when he was fired as the drug and gun charges were announced, WBUR reported. Investigators allegedly intercepted eight kilograms of cocaine that was to be delivered to the state office building where he worked, according to Boston.com. He pleaded not guilty and was released on $25,000 bail in March.
## The Federal Case
On Wednesday, Oct. 14, the office of U.S. Attorney Leah Foley charged Cook with one count of SNAP fraud and one count of wire fraud, Axios Boston reported.

Prosecutors allege that Cook applied for Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits on April 6, reporting no income and $100 in the bank, when at least one of his accounts held more than $8,800, WBUR reported. He has allegedly received more than $500 a month in benefits since.

According to prosecutors, as reported by WBUR and Axios, the application listed only Cook's child as a member of the household, though he lived with his fiancée, a Springfield Public Schools employee earning more than $80,000 a year, and her mother. A USDA special agent wrote that her income "should have been disclosed," Axios reported.

Prosecutors also allege that around the time he was collecting benefits, Cook received about $12,000 in Zelle payments from his mother, who had recently won $1 million in the state lottery, plus $2,497.88 in tax refunds, WBUR reported. He allegedly used his EBT card for groceries on a July trip to Florida and spent $1,904 on flights to Orlando for eight people, according to Axios.
> "I find it disturbing that the Commonwealth of Massachusetts could not prevent this from happening." — U.S. Attorney Leah Foley, as quoted by WBUR
Foley called the alleged conduct "egregious," WBUR reported. The charges are allegations; Cook has not been convicted.
## The Vacation Payout

The federal complaint comes on top of a separate dispute over money Cook received after he was fired. He was paid his $130,227 salary and $22,374.29 in accrued vacation pay, WBUR reported. The state later called the vacation payout an error but could not recover it because his account did not have the funds, and Attorney General Andrea Campbell sued in January to get it back.

In a Facebook post about the coverage, Cook used the phrase "welfare golden parachute" and described the money as a mix of earned vacation pay, his mother's lottery winnings and an EBT card, according to Axios.
## Back in Custody

Cook appeared in federal court in Boston on Wednesday and was released on personal recognizance, Boston.com reported. The next day, Hampden County prosecutors asked a state court to revoke his bail in the drug case, arguing that the new charges broke a release condition requiring him to obey federal law.

"We're here because Mr. Cook committed more crimes," Hampden County District Attorney Kerry Beattie said, according to Boston.com. Defense attorney Kedar Ismail argued that the federal charges were only allegations. "This is some type of stretch," he said. Judge David Hodge revoked Cook's bail and ordered him held for 90 days.
## The Political Response

The arrest came one day before the final governor's debate. Healey said SNAP is a federal program and that she was glad the U.S. attorney's office was prosecuting, Axios reported. Republican nominee Mike Minogue said "there was no accountability." On the debate stage Healey said she fired Cook immediately; afterward she said, "I wish I never hired LaMar Cook," NBC Boston reported.

blue-hill-avenue-center-bus-lanes-pushba.title: Boston Moves Ahead on Blue Hill Avenue Center Bus Lanes Despite Opposition
blue-hill-avenue-center-bus-lanes-pushba.dek: The Wu administration is pressing on with a $163 million redesign that would put bus-only lanes down the middle of Blue Hill Avenue, while a city councilor, a state representative and some business owners object.
body: Blue Hill Avenue runs through Mattapan, Dorchester and Roxbury, and residents have complained for years about its traffic, its dangerous crossings and its slow buses. The plan to fix it has now become a political fight of its own.
The city is going ahead with center-running bus lanes along about three miles of the avenue, WBUR reported on Oct. 15, despite opposition from some elected officials and residents.
## The Plan

The lanes are part of a roughly $163 million rebuild of Blue Hill Avenue between Mattapan Square and Grove Hall, according to WBUR. Federal grants would pay for more than half; the most recent, $80 million, came through in March.

Two lanes in the middle of the road would be reserved for buses and emergency vehicles. Bus stops would move from the sidewalks to concrete platforms in the center of the street. The plan also calls for new crosswalks, signals and sidewalks, new trees and 42 parking spaces.

At a Sept. 30 public meeting, Wu said the design would cut bus travel time on the corridor nearly in half, with buses every three to six minutes, WBUR reported. Interim Chief of Streets Chris Osgood said the plan reflects resident feedback collected since 2019.
Design is about a third done. Officials hope to show updated plans before December; construction would not begin before 2028 and could last up to three years, according to WBUR.
## The Opposition

Before the Sept. 30 town hall, state Rep. Christopher Worrell helped organize a protest of about a dozen people at the Grove Hall Mecca, WBUR reported. He argued that center bus stops would force riders, children and seniors among them, to cross two lanes of traffic to reach a bus.

City Councilor Miniard Culpepper, who represents District 7 in Roxbury, opposes the center lanes and wants the city and the MBTA to look at extending the Orange Line instead. In September his office announced a trip to Washington to press the idea with the Senate Banking Committee and with the offices of Sen. Elizabeth Warren and Rep. Ayanna Pressley, Universal Hub reported. He and District 4 Councilor Brian Worrell have proposed an Orange Line branch from Ruggles toward Mattapan Square.
Universal Hub noted that when the elevated Washington Street line came down in the 1980s, Roxbury was promised comparable rapid-transit service, and it never came.

Peter Papadogiannis, who has owned Boulevard Cleaners in Mattapan since the early 1980s, told WBUR he fears competition for parking and the construction will drive customers away, and that he might have to close within months of work starting. A Change.org petition opposes the center lanes.
## The Supporters

Transit advocates have released a joint statement supporting the design. Katarina Torres-Radisic of Transportation for Massachusetts told WBUR the plan would shorten bus trips and make the corridor fully accessible to people with disabilities for the first time. Resident Grace Richardson thanked the mayor for addressing what she called historical disinvestment in Boston's Black community.
The most recent public comment period on the design closed the week of Oct. 12, according to WBUR.

healey-responds-to-alleged-rape-inside-s.title: Healey Criticized Over Debate Response to Vineyard Barracks Rape Case
healey-responds-to-alleged-rape-inside-s.dek: Victim advocates and her Republican challenger faulted Gov. Maura Healey's debate remarks about a rape allegation at a State Police barracks on Martha's Vineyard.
body: Gov. Maura Healey was criticized after she said during a Thursday night debate that sometimes things happen, when she was asked about misconduct in the State Police following a rape allegation at the agency's Martha's Vineyard barracks, the Boston Globe reported.

In the Oct. 15 debate with Republican challenger Michael Minogue, Healey said she and State Police Col. Geoffrey D. Noble make sure swift action is taken, and said she is proud of the State Police and that Noble is doing a good job, according to the Globe.

The case involves Edward J. Brown, 27, a Boston Public Schools security official who was arrested Oct. 9 at Boston Latin Academy. He is charged with raping a woman he brought to the barracks, where he was staying as a trooper's guest. Brown pleaded not guilty Tuesday in Edgartown District Court, the Globe reported, and he is presumed innocent.

Amanda Walsh of the Victim Rights Law Center told the Globe that the governor missed a chance to reassure survivors. Minogue called the response unacceptable. Healey pointed out that Brown is a civilian, not a member of the State Police, and in a separate statement called the alleged assault a horrific crime and said there is zero tolerance for such conduct.
State Police have opened an internal affairs investigation, and Noble has barred overnight guests at temporary trooper housing on Martha's Vineyard and Nantucket, according to the Globe.

wu-proposes-free-city-run-shuttles-to-ex.title: Boston to Launch Five Free City-Run Shuttle Routes in Early 2027
wu-proposes-free-city-run-shuttles-to-ex.dek: Mayor Michelle Wu's Link Bus Program, paid for with an $11.5 million federal grant, would connect neighborhoods to transit stops for three years.
body: Boston plans to start five free shuttle bus routes linking residential neighborhoods with public transit, Mayor Michelle Wu's administration announced, according to Boston.com.

The Link Bus Program will serve Mattapan, Roxbury, Allston-Brighton, Charlestown and the Lower Mystic, and the Seaport, the city said. The routes are meant to close what are called first-mile and last-mile gaps between where riders start or end their trips and the transit system.

The money is $11.5 million from the Federal Highway Administration's Congestion Relief Program, enough to run the shuttles for three years, according to the city. The Economic Development and Industrial Corporation of Boston voted to accept it at its Sept. 17 meeting. Service is expected to start in early 2027, and schedules and routes will be posted on the city's website then.

The Allston-Brighton, Charlestown and Lower Mystic, and Seaport routes will be run with existing local transportation organizations, Boston.com reported. The Mattapan and Roxbury routes are not final; the city is working with residents on destinations and will pick operators through competitive procurement.

Wu said the program would bring free transportation into neighborhoods and strengthen links to the MBTA. The city said it will look for ways to keep the service going after the three-year grant runs out.

wu-endorses-healey-for-re-election.title: Mayor Wu Endorses Gov. Healey and Lt. Gov. Driscoll for Re-Election
wu-endorses-healey-for-re-election.dek: Boston Mayor Michelle Wu formally backed the Healey-Driscoll ticket on Thursday, citing their work together on transit, housing and public safety.
body: Boston Mayor Michelle Wu formally endorsed Gov. Maura Healey and Lt. Gov. Kim Driscoll for re-election on Thursday morning, according to WBUR, which published a State House News Service report by Colin A. Young.

In announcing it, Wu spoke of a partnership to build a city and state that work for everyone, the report said. She thanked the Healey administration for its work on lowering costs, housing, public safety and opportunity, and said she looks forward to continuing that work. On WBUR's Morning Edition, Wu also discussed the endorsement and pointed to the two leaders' work together on the MBTA and commuter rail.

Healey answered by calling Wu a fantastic partner and a champion for Boston residents, according to the report. She pointed to the summer's events in the city, the World Cup among them, and said she was grateful to work with the mayor.

Both Democrats are the first women elected to their offices, but WBUR reported they are not known for a close political relationship. Last month they backed opposing candidates in two Democratic state Senate primaries, and on the eve of Wu's 2025 mayoral primary against Josh Kraft, Healey declined to say whether she supported Wu, according to the report.

Mike Minogue, the Republican candidate for governor, posted a video on social media Tuesday mocking Healey and Wu, recalling the two being booed at Fenway Park in April, WBUR reported. Healey and Wu were scheduled to appear together Thursday at Otis Elementary School in East Boston to mark upgrades to the school building.

third-party-transfer-60-million-settleme.title: City Agrees to $60 Million Settlement Over Homes Taken Through Third Party Transfer
third-party-transfer-60-million-settleme.dek: New York City has agreed to a proposed $60 million settlement with residents who lost ownership of their homes through the Third Party Transfer program, ABC7 New York's 7 On Your Side Investigates reported on Oct. 19.
body: Isabel Adon bought into a Bronx co-op on Nelson Avenue in the late 1970s. In 2018, she and dozens of other families in the building stopped being owners. With little or no notice and no payment, they became renters in apartments they had bought, according to an investigation by ABC7 New York's 7 On Your Side.
> "That was the legacy for my kids." — Isabel Adon
## How a Building Changes Hands

The mechanism was a city program called Third Party Transfer. Under it, New York identifies buildings it considers distressed, meaning they have physical and financial problems, and transfers the deed to a nonprofit to run, ABC7 reported. Over roughly three decades and several rounds, the city used the process on more than 500 properties.

A City Council investigation found that most of those properties were in minority communities, and that half of the properties chosen were not distressed under the legal definition, according to the station.

The owners lost more than a deed. Residents told ABC7 they saw the transfers as a theft of generational wealth. Junior Gonzalez, a Marine Corps veteran who also bought into the Nelson Avenue building, lost his ownership as well.
## Seven Years in Court

In 2019, attorneys Yolande Nicholson and Matthew L. Berman filed a federal lawsuit arguing that the transfers violated the constitutional protection against the government taking private property for public use without just compensation, ABC7 reported. Other law firms joined the case later.

After about seven years of litigation, the city agreed to a proposed $60 million settlement, which ABC7 called one of the largest local civil rights settlements in recent history. It covers only the hundreds of people affected by the latest round of transfers, not everyone who lost property under the program. It still needs a judge's approval and the residents' sign-off, and could be resolved by next summer.
Gonzalez was plain about the deal, telling ABC7 that the plaintiffs are not jumping for joy.
## What Happens to the Program

The city says the program was run under earlier administrations. A spokesperson for the Department of Housing Preservation and Development told ABC7 that the Mamdani administration and the City Council are working to update and strengthen Third Party Transfer to address the concerns raised in the lawsuits.
The plaintiffs' lawyers want it ended. Berman argued that eminent domain, which requires compensation, is the right tool when the government wants property for policy goals like these, ABC7 reported.
Nicholson told the station she hopes the case and the settlement become a catalyst for change.

For families like Adon's, any payment would come decades after the purchase and years after the deed was transferred. Whether City Hall keeps some version of the program will decide whether other owners lose their homes the same way.

suspicious-powder-ritchie-torres-bronx-o.title: Suspicious Powder Mailed to Rep. Ritchie Torres' Bronx Office, Six Exposed
suspicious-powder-ritchie-torres-bronx-o.dek: An envelope containing a suspicious powder exposed six people at Rep. Ritchie Torres' Fordham Road district office on Oct. 16, a day after suspicious mail was sent to Sens. Chuck Schumer and Kirsten Gillibrand.
body: The envelope came to 540 East Fordham Road, Rep. Ritchie Torres' district office in the Bronx, on Friday, Oct. 16. The FDNY was called at 1:23 p.m., according to amNY.

It held a suspicious powder. Six people were exposed, the FDNY said, and hazardous materials units went to the block between Lorillard Place and Bathgate Avenue, one of the busiest commercial strips in the borough.
## Not Hazardous

Tests found the substance was not hazardous, and an FDNY spokesperson reported no injuries, amNY reported. Torres' staff notified the FBI, the NYPD and the FDNY, and the envelope was handed over to the FBI. The investigation is continuing.
Torres wrote on X that his office had received an envelope containing a suspicious substance, and that his team was shaken but would not be deterred from serving the 15th Congressional District.
> "The new normal." — Rep. Ritchie Torres, on threats against officials and staff
## A Series of Mailings

The Bronx scare came a day after suspicious mail was sent to two of New York's most senior Democrats. On Thursday, Oct. 15, suspicious mail went to Sen. Chuck Schumer and Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand, amNY reported. The Washington Post reported that Schumer was among several senators whose offices were targeted. The U.S. Postal Inspection Service intercepted the mail addressed to Gillibrand's New York City office, and Gillibrand thanked postal inspectors for protecting her staff.

The FBI and the Postal Inspection Service are investigating a string of suspicious mailings around the country, including letters to secretaries of state and election offices, some of which held an unknown substance, according to amNY. The FBI would not say whether the Torres envelope is part of that investigation.
## Weeks Before the Vote

The mailings came as New York enters the last weeks of a close governor's race between Gov. Kathy Hochul and Republican Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman, with early voting about to open and Election Day on Nov. 3.

Election offices have been among the targets nationally, a concern for the workers who staff them. For the six people exposed on Fordham Road, the tests came back clear. As of Oct. 16, the FBI had not said who sent the envelope.

mamdani-hochul-ad-blakeman-bad-apple.title: Mamdani Appears in Hochul Ad Calling Blakeman 'a Bad Apple'
mamdani-hochul-ad-blakeman-bad-apple.dek: Gov. Kathy Hochul's campaign released a video on Oct. 15 in which Mayor Zohran Mamdani criticizes Republican Bruce Blakeman on Medicaid, child care and ICE, as both candidates made their last pitches before early voting.
body: For most of the campaign, the question in Albany was whether New York City's democratic socialist mayor would help the governor or hurt her. On Thursday, Oct. 15, Gov. Kathy Hochul's campaign gave its answer by putting Mayor Zohran Mamdani in front of the camera, according to amNY.

The video, about a minute long and also posted as an Instagram reel, argues that Republican nominee Bruce Blakeman, the Nassau County executive, would make life harder for working New Yorkers. It ends with Mamdani calling Blakeman a bad apple.
## Three Lines of Attack

The ad puts together clips of Blakeman on three issues, amNY reported. On Medicaid, it uses an earlier clip of Blakeman saying the goal was to cut Medicaid in half, two days after he said in Tuesday's televised debate that he had never said he would.
> "I never said that I would cut Medicaid in half." — Bruce Blakeman, during the debate

On child care, the video returns to Blakeman's criticism of subsidized care for parents who are not working, including a remark in which he used a crude phrase for an unemployed parent receiving aid. On immigration, Mamdani says Blakeman would rather send money to ICE, over footage of Blakeman praising the agency's work, amNY reported. As Nassau County executive, Blakeman has cooperated with federal immigration authorities.
## Blakeman's Response

In a statement, Blakeman defended his child care remarks, saying he supports universal child care for working parents but questions paying for care for parents who do not work, amNY reported. He accused Hochul and Mamdani of making New York less affordable through taxes, utility costs and transit fares. He did not respond on the Medicaid clip.
## Asset or Liability

Speaking to reporters at an affordable housing event with Hochul in East New York, Mamdani said he expects to campaign with the governor before Election Day on Nov. 3. Asked whether he helps or hurts her, he said he believes his administration's work is an asset, amNY reported. He pointed to a $1.2 billion investment that opened 2,000 free child care seats for 2-year-olds this year, with 10,000 more expected next year.
## The Last Weekend Before Early Voting

By Sunday, Oct. 18, the two candidates were at opposite ends of the region. Hochul campaigned in Concourse Village in the Bronx, pointing to the state's ban on cell phones in schools and wider access to community college and child care, ABC7 New York reported. Local supporters told the station that turnout is still a major problem for Democrats in the borough.
Hochul told the Bronx crowd she was counting on them.

Blakeman campaigned in Elmont on Long Island with Lee Zeldin, the former congressman Hochul narrowly beat in 2022, who later became administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency under President Trump. Blakeman argued that high costs are pushing people out of the state and promised to cut taxes and utility rates. Hochul answered that New York has the fastest-growing economy in the country, ABC7 reported.
Early voting starts the following weekend.

mamdani-keeps-tisch-orders-use-of-force-.title: Mamdani Says He Will Keep Tisch as Police Commissioner Despite Calls From the Left
mamdani-keeps-tisch-orders-use-of-force-.dek: Mayor Zohran Mamdani said on Oct. 13 he has no plans to replace NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch, a day after ordering the department's first comprehensive use-of-force review in a decade.
body: In Battery Park City on Tuesday, Oct. 13, after a ceremony that added 42 names to the NYPD's Memorial Wall of fallen officers, Mayor Zohran Mamdani gave his clearest answer so far to the activists who helped elect him and now want his police commissioner out, according to ABC7 New York.
> "I have no plans to change that." — Mayor Zohran Mamdani
Mamdani credited Commissioner Jessica Tisch with rooting out corruption in the NYPD's upper ranks while bringing down crime across the city, the station reported.
## The Pressure From the Left

Some of the mayor's own supporters say his policing changes do not go far enough. The Democratic Socialists of America have accused Tisch of helping Immigration and Customs Enforcement operate in New York, a charge both Tisch and Mamdani deny, ABC7 reported.

The group has linked that accusation to the Oct. 8 ICE shooting in Marble Hill, arguing that federal agents were able to leave an Inwood hospital with the wounded man because NYPD Strategic Response Group officers cleared protesters from the street. One protester, Micaela Martinez, told the station that the NYPD is not making people feel safe at demonstrations.

Mamdani, once a sharp critic of the police, has seemed to moderate since taking office, ABC7 noted, though he has promised to dismantle the Strategic Response Group and move its focus to counterterrorism.
## The First Review in a Decade

A day earlier, on Oct. 12, Mamdani directed the NYPD to conduct its first comprehensive review of use-of-force policies and practices in a decade, ABC7 reported. The review will take place over the coming months and include community engagement on how the rules are applied and whether they should change.

The order followed scrutiny of a case in Ozone Park, Queens. In May 2024, police called to a home where a 19-year-old was reportedly in a psychiatric crisis shot him after, police said, he lunged at officers with scissors. The state attorney general cleared the officers, but the Civilian Complaint Review Board later found they used excessive force. One officer retired before facing an administrative trial because the NYPD did not tell the board his retirement was pending; Tisch called the failure an oversight, ABC7 reported.

Along with the review, the mayor announced stricter notification rules for pending retirements, more money for the inspector general who monitors the NYPD, and standardized public disclosure for police-involved incidents.
Mamdani said that when the government uses force against a New Yorker, the standard for accountability must be at its highest.
## Objections From Both Sides

Neither side was satisfied. The president of the Police Benevolent Association argued there should be no review of use-of-force rules without a matching review of how the CCRB interprets them, ABC7 reported. Scott Munro, president of the Detectives' Endowment Association, said the mayor should focus on the review board instead, arguing its staff are anti-police.
On the other side, Loyda Colon of the Justice Committee said a broader overhaul of NYPD discipline is needed and called the measures far from enough.
The department also plans to review how it responded to the hospital protests after the Marble Hill shooting, according to ABC7.

mahmoud-khalil-asks-supreme-court-to-let.title: Mahmoud Khalil Asks Supreme Court to Let Judges Review Immigration Detentions
mahmoud-khalil-asks-supreme-court-to-let.dek: The activist and former Columbia University graduate student is appealing a ruling that federal courts cannot review detentions until immigration courts finish a case.
body: Activist Mahmoud Khalil asked the U.S. Supreme Court on Monday to let federal judges decide quickly whether immigration detentions are lawful, so that people are not held for months or years with no judicial review, the Associated Press reported in a story published by NY1.

In court papers, Khalil asked the justices to overturn a ruling issued earlier this year by the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in Philadelphia. That court held that federal courts have no jurisdiction to review whether a detention is legal until immigration courts have fully considered the case, according to the AP.

Khalil, a lawful permanent resident and former Columbia University graduate student, was detained by immigration authorities in 2025 over his part in pro-Palestinian demonstrations at Columbia in spring 2024. The government argued then that his presence harmed U.S. foreign policy interests. He was held for more than three months before a federal judge in New Jersey ordered him released, finding the government had acted unconstitutionally, the AP reported.
The Department of Homeland Security said Monday that the administration acted within its legal authority, and urged Khalil to self-deport using the CBP Home app.

The 3rd Circuit has put its ruling on hold while Khalil appeals, and he remains free. Separately, the government has asked the Supreme Court to overturn a conflicting 4th Circuit decision that upheld the release of Georgetown University scholar Badar Khan Suri. According to the AP, conflicting appeals court rulings can make it more likely that the court takes a case; if it does, arguments would probably be heard next year.

citys-2-k-child-care-program-to-expand-t.title: City's Free 2-K Program to Expand to All Five Boroughs Next Fall
citys-2-k-child-care-program-to-expand-t.dek: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Gov. Kathy Hochul said more than 12,000 children will have access to free 2-K, up from about 2,000 seats this year.
body: New York City's free 2-K program for 2-year-olds will reach all five boroughs next fall, including every school district in the Bronx and on Staten Island, Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Gov. Kathy Hochul announced Monday, NY1 reported.

More than 12,000 children will have access, up from about 2,000 who got seats in this year's first rollout, Mamdani said at a news conference. After the expansion, 22 of the city's 32 school districts will take part, according to NY1. The mayor said the program will save parents more than $25,000 per child per year.

According to the mayor's office, the expansion adds seats in Manhattan, Brooklyn and Queens and increases capacity in the five districts where 2-K started: District 6 in Manhattan, District 10 in the Bronx, Districts 18 and 23 in Brooklyn and District 27 in Queens. The new districts are Districts 4 and 5 in Manhattan; Districts 16, 17, 19, 20, 21 and 32 in Brooklyn; and Districts 24, 28 and 29 in Queens.
Mamdani said families across the city would feel relief when placements are announced next year, and that the city should remain affordable for people raising children.

The expansion is part of the administration's wider child care effort. Earlier this month, the city moved more than 10,000 children off a waitlist for free child care vouchers, NY1 reported. The city said it will release the 2-K application timeline in the coming weeks.

mamdani-replaces-four-members-of-nypd-ci.title: Mamdani Replaces Four Members of NYPD Civilian Complaint Review Board
mamdani-replaces-four-members-of-nypd-ci.dek: The mayor named four new appointees to the Civilian Complaint Review Board, the independent agency that investigates complaints of police misconduct.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced Monday that he is replacing four of his five appointees to the Civilian Complaint Review Board, the city agency that investigates complaints of police misconduct and recommends discipline, amNewYork reported.

The new members are Reginald Greene, Lisa Hoyes, Lisa Landau and Wesner Pierre, according to amNY. Among them they have worked in criminal prosecution at the Manhattan District Attorney's Office, federal public defense, health law and youth violence prevention. They replace John Siegal, Pat Smith, Sherene Crawford and Rahul Agarwal, changes City Hall confirmed to the outlet. June Northern, appointed by former Mayor Eric Adams in 2023, stays on the board, which also has members chosen by the City Council, the public advocate and the police commissioner.

In a statement, Mamdani said public safety depends on accountability and that the new members would strengthen public trust. CCRB Chair Jennifer Jones Austin, whom Mamdani named in July as the board's first permanent chair in nearly six years, welcomed the new members and thanked those leaving.

The appointments come after Mamdani announced earlier this month the NYPD's first comprehensive review of its use-of-force policies in a decade. That review followed the retirement, with a disability pension, of an officer involved in a fatal 2024 police shooting in Queens before he faced a disciplinary trial; Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch apologized for the department's failure to notify the CCRB, amNY reported.

Police unions criticized the changes. PBA President Patrick Hendry called for a review of how the CCRB interprets use-of-force policies, and Detectives' Endowment Association President Scott Munro accused the mayor of empowering a board he called anti-police.

blakeman-calls-hochul-a-useful-tool-who-.title: Blakeman Says Hochul Takes Orders From Mamdani in Closing Pitch
blakeman-calls-hochul-a-useful-tool-who-.dek: Republican nominee Bruce Blakeman attacked Gov. Kathy Hochul's ties to Mayor Zohran Mamdani in an interview on public safety, taxes and utility costs.
body: Republican gubernatorial nominee Bruce Blakeman said Gov. Kathy Hochul takes orders from Mayor Zohran Mamdani and called her a "useful tool" of what he described as an anti-American movement in the Democratic Party, Hoodline reported, citing a New York Post interview.

Blakeman, the Nassau County executive, spoke in a 20-minute interview presented as a closing argument on public safety, taxes and utility costs, with a little more than two weeks left before the Nov. 3 election. Early voting starts Oct. 24.

The remarks came after Mamdani released a campaign video on Oct. 15 supporting Hochul, in which he criticized Blakeman on Medicaid, child care and cooperation with ICE, according to amNY. The video cited a past Blakeman pledge to cut Medicaid spending in half; at the Oct. 13 debate, Blakeman said he never made that statement. He said he supports universal child care for working parents but questioned paying for care for people who do not work.

In the interview, Blakeman said he would cut income taxes, end green-energy policies in order to expand energy supply, natural gas included, and try to cut utility bills in half, Hoodline reported. He also said he would push to end congestion pricing and fill NYPD vacancies. He has previously outlined plans for surveillance cameras, license-plate readers and facial-recognition technology along the border between Nassau and New York City, according to Newsday.
Blakeman disputed polls that show him behind and called the race close. Mamdani told amNY he expects to campaign with Hochul before Election Day.

mta-watchdog-bronx-subway-shop-roofs-end.title: MTA Inspector General Finds Dangerous Roof Damage at Two Bronx Subway Shops
mta-watchdog-bronx-subway-shop-roofs-end.dek: A report found water leaked onto a crane's electrical system for about 15 years at the East 180th Street shop and concrete fell inside the 240th Street shop.
body: The roofs of two Bronx subway maintenance shops are dangerously compromised after years of repair requests that went unaddressed, according to a report by the MTA Office of the Inspector General, Hoodline reported, citing the New York Daily News.

At the East 180th Street Yard Maintenance Shop, which maintains cars for the 2 and 5 trains, plants grow out of cracks in the roof and rainwater has leaked into the electrical distribution room, the report found. For about 15 years, water dripped from the roof onto a crane's high-voltage electrical system, making the crane unsafe in wet weather and holding up some repairs. A former head of the shop told investigators the roof looked almost the same in 2014.

At the 240th Street Yard Maintenance Shop, which services 1 train cars, water getting in has caused chunks of reinforced concrete to fall into the shop, according to the report. NYC Transit's car equipment division has proposed replacing that roof several times since 1984. Investigators also found that the MTA's capital plan did not always reflect real conditions, and that staff inspected structures without specialized training.

The MTA has emergency repairs in progress and has made temporary fixes at both shops, according to Hoodline. The agency agreed with all of the inspector general's recommendations, including better inspections and trained assessors. NYC Transit has created a facilities division whose roof team has finished seven repairs so far.

Both shops are scheduled for major overhauls under the MTA's 2025-2029 capital program. Transit officials told WNYC the shops must be rebuilt before the agency can replace the aging R62 subway cars on the 1 and 3 lines.

blakeman-uses-fatal-subway-shooting-to-a.title: Blakeman Uses Fatal Midtown Subway Shooting to Attack Hochul
blakeman-uses-fatal-subway-shooting-to-a.dek: The Republican nominee for governor rode the subway to the station where a man was killed, while Hochul's campaign pointed to state spending on subway policing.
body: Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman on Monday used a fatal weekend shooting at a Midtown subway station to criticize Gov. Kathy Hochul's record on public safety, NY1 reported.

Blakeman took the subway from his Long Island home to the Seventh Avenue station near West 53rd Street, where police say an argument between two men ended with a 26-year-old man shot dead, according to NY1. The suspect had not been caught when NY1 published its report.

Blakeman accused Hochul of pulling police off subway platforms and called for more officers in the system, better lighting at the station and more conductors on trains, NY1 reported. He told reporters that a police presence might have deterred the attack.

Hochul's campaign pointed to two years of state money set aside for NYPD overtime and overnight subway patrols, according to NY1. A campaign spokeswoman said the governor had invested a record $4 billion in policing. Mayor Zohran Mamdani, at a separate event in the Bronx, accused Blakeman of exploiting New Yorkers' fears for political gain.
NYPD officials have pointed to overall drops in crime, including on the subway, but seven deaths have been recorded in the system this year, compared with four last year, NY1 reported.

investigation-details-hourslong-ordeal-f.title: Investigation Details Hourslong Ordeal for Six Nonverbal Students on School Bus
investigation-details-hourslong-ordeal-f.dek: A school bus carrying six nonverbal students with special needs went to the wrong locations around Brooklyn and arrived more than four hours late, a city investigator found, NY1 reported.
body: Six nonverbal students with special needs, ages 6 to 8, were unaccounted for for more than four hours last year after their school bus was driven to the wrong locations around Brooklyn, according to a report by the city's Special Commissioner of Investigation for the public schools, NY1 reported.
