The students were expected at school around 9 a.m. and did not arrive until about 1:25 p.m., the outlet said. A parent who had put tracking devices in her two children's backpacks followed the bus and called repeatedly for information. School officials contacted the bus company at 10 a.m., and at 11:45 a.m. the company said the driver was lost but would arrive within 15 minutes. The bus arrived about an hour and 40 minutes after that, after police had been called.

The driver was a fill-in with less than three weeks on the job, and the matron had nearly 20 years in the role; both worked for Consolidated Bus Transit, according to the report. The driver told investigators he went to two wrong schools before getting the right address and was held up by phone calls. The matron said she did not speak with the driver or try to reach anyone.

Special Commissioner Anastasia Coleman said the incident was serious enough to call for a formal investigation, which recommended that the two employees no longer work with Department of Education students. The company told the Daily News that both had been placed on administrative leave; it did not respond to NY1.
The city's yellow bus system carries about 150,000 children, nearly 70,000 of them with disabilities, NY1 reported.

democratic-governors-group-spends-4-3m-t.title: Democratic Governors-Backed Super PAC Puts $4.3 Million Behind Hochul
democratic-governors-group-spends-4-3m-t.dek: A super PAC backed by the Democratic Governors Association has spent $4.3 million supporting Gov. Kathy Hochul's reelection bid against Republican Bruce Blakeman.
body: Greater Empire State, a super PAC backed by the Democratic Governors Association, has put $4.3 million behind Gov. Kathy Hochul's reelection campaign, according to Hoodline, citing reporting by the New York Post. The group's first general-election TV ads, which aired Saturday, portray Republican nominee Bruce Blakeman as aligned with President Trump's agenda.

State filings show the PAC raised about $4.34 million from late July to Oct. 2, Hoodline reported. Donors listed include former Mayor Michael Bloomberg and the Greater New York Hospital Association Management Corp., at $1 million each, a $1 million transfer from the super PAC Leadership for New York, and $600,000 from the Sports Betting Alliance.

According to Newsday, as cited by Hoodline, the association joined the 2022 race less than a week before Election Day; this year its PAC started in the summer. Separately, the state Democratic Committee gave Hochul's campaign $10 million in September. On the other side, a pro-Blakeman super PAC has been spending $750,000 a week on TV ads attacking a COVID-19 testing contract awarded under Hochul, Hoodline reported.

Hochul's campaign declined to comment on the spending, according to the Post. A Blakeman spokesperson said the late money shows Democratic desperation and that voters are ready to reject Hochul over taxes and utility bills.

The polls cited in the report do not agree. An October Marist poll of registered voters had Hochul ahead 53 percent to 42 percent, while a Pollfinity survey released Tuesday showed Blakeman behind by 3 points.

bloomberg-backed-charter-pac-pours-1-8m-.title: Bloomberg-Funded Charter School PAC Launches Campaign Backing Hochul
bloomberg-backed-charter-pac-pours-1-8m-.dek: New Yorkers for a Balanced Albany, a pro-charter super PAC that received $1.8 million from Michael Bloomberg this year, is spending seven figures to reelect Gov. Kathy Hochul.
body: A pro-charter school super PAC funded by former Mayor Michael Bloomberg is spending seven figures on a get-out-the-vote and media campaign to reelect Gov. Kathy Hochul, Hoodline reported, citing the New York Post, which first reported the plans.

Bloomberg has given the group, New Yorkers for a Balanced Albany, $1.8 million this year, according to the Post. The PAC is also supporting seven moderate Democratic state Senate candidates in competitive districts on Long Island, in the Lower Hudson Valley and the Capital Region, and in southern Brooklyn and Staten Island.
Crystal McQueen-Taylor, a spokesperson for the group, said Hochul has stood up for students and families and that parents are now canvassing for her in Brooklyn, Harlem and the Bronx.

The pro-charter group StudentsFirstNY created the PAC in 2014. According to City & State New York, as cited by Hoodline, it first helped Senate Republicans keep control of the chamber, then after 2019 moved to supporting pro-charter moderate Democrats. Separately, Bloomberg gave $1 million to the pro-Hochul Empire State PAC in September, and his representatives would not say whether he plans to spend more.

The spending comes as Hochul announced that New York would opt into a new federal tax credit scholarship program, which the state teachers union opposed. On the other side, a super PAC supporting Republican Bruce Blakeman, funded in part by James Dolan and Steve Wynn, started a $750,000-a-week ad campaign this month. The election is Nov. 3.

suspicious-powder-mailed-to-rep-ritchie-.title: Suspicious Powder Mailed to Rep. Ritchie Torres' Bronx Office
suspicious-powder-mailed-to-rep-ritchie-.dek: Six people were reportedly exposed to a substance later found to be non-hazardous, and the FBI is investigating.
body: An envelope containing a suspicious powder brought a hazardous materials response to U.S. Rep. Ritchie Torres' district office on East Fordham Road in the Bronx on Friday afternoon, amNY reported.

The FDNY got a call at 1:23 p.m. on Oct. 16 about the powder at 540 East Fordham Road and sent hazmat units, according to amNY. The department said six people were reportedly exposed. A spokesperson said the substance was found to be non-hazardous and no injuries were reported.

Torres said his staff notified the FBI, the NYPD and the FDNY right away, and the envelope was given to the FBI, amNY reported. In a post on X, he said his team was shaken but would not be deterred, and he described threats against elected officials and their staff as a new normal.

It happened a day after suspicious mail was sent to the New York offices of Sens. Chuck Schumer and Kirsten Gillibrand, according to amNY. The FBI said it and the Postal Inspection Service are investigating suspicious mailings sent around the country, some of them containing an unknown substance.
The FBI would not confirm whether the Torres envelope belongs to that series. The investigation is continuing.

mamdani-asks-parking-lot-and-garage-owne.title: Mamdani Asks Parking Lot and Garage Owners to Deny ICE Access
mamdani-asks-parking-lot-and-garage-owne.dek: The mayor and more than 100 elected officials urged private operators not to let immigration agents use their properties as staging areas, NY1 reported.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani, at the head of a coalition of more than 100 state elected officials, has sent a letter asking private parking lot and garage operators in the five boroughs to keep federal immigration agents from using their properties as staging areas, according to NY1.

The letter asks owners not to rent, lend or otherwise make their facilities available to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, and to tell the agency directly that it may not use them, the outlet reported.

The request follows the Oct. 8 shooting in Marble Hill, in which an ICE agent shot a 28-year-old man while his young son was in the car, NY1 reported. According to the mayor's office, agents had been using a privately owned parking lot a few blocks away as a staging area. The letter also cited reports of ICE using two bank parking lots on Northern Boulevard in Queens and a garage on Morton Street in Manhattan.

Mamdani argued that immigrants are more than a third of the city's population and 43% of its workforce, and that businesses suffer when residents are afraid to drive or run errands, according to the report. He praised the Morton Street garage operator for removing ICE vehicles after neighbors raised concerns.

City law already limits the use of city-owned property for federal civil immigration enforcement, but those limits do not apply the same way to private property, the mayor's office said. NY1's report did not include a response from ICE or from parking industry representatives.

mamdani-cuts-ad-backing-hochuls-reelecti.title: Mamdani Appears in Ad Backing Hochul's Reelection Bid
mamdani-cuts-ad-backing-hochuls-reelecti.dek: The mayor's ad for Gov. Kathy Hochul criticizes Republican Bruce Blakeman on federal spending cuts, ICE and universal child care.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani appears in a new ad for Gov. Kathy Hochul's reelection campaign, released Thursday, NY1 reported.

In it, Mamdani says he is voting for Hochul because she is "the real deal for New Yorkers" and calls her Republican opponent, Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman, "a bad apple," according to NY1. The ad says Blakeman believes a trillion dollars in federal cuts did not go far enough and would rather send money to ICE, and says he opposes universal child care. It also points to the mayor and governor's work together on the city budget and affordability.
In a statement to NY1, Blakeman said Hochul and Mamdani cannot be trusted. He said he supports universal child care for working parents but questioned paying for care for people who are not working.

The ad came out the same day as an event in East New York, where Hochul, Mamdani and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries opened new housing. The first phase of the Innovative Urban Village project brings 386 affordable units to the neighborhood, according to NY1. There, Hochul said Albany and the city are aligned on affordability through housing.
Mamdani is expected to campaign with Hochul in the city in the last weeks of the race, NY1 reported.

queens-officials-renew-calls-to-abolish-.title: Queens Officials Renew Calls to Abolish ICE After Marble Hill Shooting
queens-officials-renew-calls-to-abolish-.dek: Democratic lawmakers in Queens called for ICE to be abolished after federal agents shot a 28-year-old man in Marble Hill, while a Republican council member defended the arrest.
body: Elected officials across Queens renewed calls to abolish U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement after federal agents shot a 28-year-old man in his car in Marble Hill on Oct. 8, QNS reported. The man's young son was in the car.

ICE and federal officials say the man refused an order to get out of the vehicle and tried to use it against agents, a claim critics dispute, according to QNS. The NYPD said at least one agent fired seven shots, hitting the man in the neck. A federal judge in Brooklyn has temporarily blocked his deportation and ordered authorities to explain why he should not be released.

Assembly Member Jessica González-Rojas called the shooting terrifying and said she fears similar incidents in Corona, Elmhurst and Jackson Heights. She and Assembly member-elect Brian Romero said stepped-up ICE activity has hurt local businesses, and alleged that some businesses had let agents use their parking lots. Neither business named in the report responded to QNS.

Council Member Julie Won urged Mayor Zohran Mamdani to fire Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch after officers clashed with protesters, and to disband the NYPD's Strategic Response Group. Council Member Tiffany Cabán also called for ICE to be abolished. Mamdani has said he has no plans to fire Tisch, citing record-low crime, a decision Gov. Kathy Hochul called smart.
Republican Council Member Joann Ariola rejected the push to abolish ICE and said the arrest was justified, according to QNS.

hochul-backs-mamdanis-decision-to-keep-t.title: Hochul Backs Mamdani's Decision to Keep Tisch as Police Commissioner
hochul-backs-mamdanis-decision-to-keep-t.dek: Gov. Kathy Hochul called it a smart decision for Mayor Zohran Mamdani to keep NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch despite calls from the Democratic Socialists of America to fire her.
body: Gov. Kathy Hochul said Mayor Zohran Mamdani made a "smart decision" in rejecting calls to fire NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch, amNewYork reported. Hochul spoke at an event in Jackson Heights, Queens.

Parts of Mamdani's political base, including the city chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America, have called for Tisch's removal over the NYPD's response to the Oct. 8 shooting of a 28-year-old man by an ICE officer in Marble Hill, according to amNY. The DSA chapter alleged that officers clashed violently with protesters after the shooting. Other critics alleged that the NYPD helped ICE leave a hospital with the man in custody, which they said broke the city's sanctuary laws.

Mamdani told reporters Tuesday that he has no plans to fire Tisch, citing record-low crime and her work rooting out corruption in the department's upper ranks. Hochul said she supports that decision, praised Tisch's leadership and pointed to a drop in crime, amNY reported. She called the matter closed.

The pressure from the left has not stopped. Congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier, whom Mamdani endorsed, alleged that officers shoved her to the ground during the protests and called for Tisch's removal. Seventeen socialist state lawmakers and Democratic nominees signed a letter calling for Tisch to be fired unless she disbands the NYPD's Strategic Response Group and ends what they called assistance to ICE.
The article did not include responses from the NYPD, Tisch or ICE. Tisch was still commissioner as of publication.
